- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to under-forecast; increase forecast by 15–30% for near-term (1–7d) horizon.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model over-forecasts; reduce forecast by 20–40% for medium-term (8–30d) horizon.
- After sharp price spikes (true outcome > 2x recent mean), model often overshoots; apply “lag correction” — reduce forecast by 30–50% for 1–3d after spike.
- If sentiment history shows repeated mean reversion (e.g., 3+ consecutive 0.00 or -0.33), model over-anticipates reversal; dampen forecast for 7–14d horizon.
- For 30d horizon, if true outcome is > 3x historical 30d mean, model under-estimates; apply “long-term bias correction” — add 20–40% to forecast if sentiment is neutral or positive.
- If sentiment is flat (0.33–0.67) and price is trending, model often misses momentum; increase forecast by 10–20% for 1–14d horizon.
